meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (national unitary company-law jurisdiction; no sub-state incorporation registry for the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental legal system; commercial statutes centralized under the Código de Comercio of 1885 and the consolidated Ley de Sociedades de Capital; foral regional civil-law specialities in Navarra and Aragón do not affect corporate form or name clearance)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Central America Association Agreement (in force since 2013; includes investment-protection provisions)
EU-Mexico Global Agreement (in force since 2000; modernisation agreed in principle in 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Exact legal matrix: (i) Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (arts. 6-10 and 22-24 on denomination, registered office, incorporation deed and capital); (ii) Real Decreto 421/2015, de 29 de mayo, por el que se regulan determinadas materias de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (incorporation formalities and registry filings); (iii) Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, aprobado por Real Decreto 1784/1996, de 19 de julio (denomination certificates and registry books); (iv) Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as last amended by Real Decreto-ley 7/2021 (arts. 1-4, 11-14, 30-31 and 53); (v) Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010 (arts. 11-17 on beneficial-owner identification and risk assessment); (vi) Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio, por el que se regula el Registro de Titularidades Reales; (vii) Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 (travel rule) and Directives (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843, as transposed; (viii) FATF Recommendations 10, 12, 24 and 25 and the 2017 Mutual Evaluation of Spain
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted-access register: not openly searchable by the general public; access is granted only to competent authorities such as SEPBLAC, Agencia Tributaria, police and law-enforcement bodies, plus obliged AML/CFT entities, notaries and registrars with a demonstrable legitimate interest, pursuant to Ley 10/2010 arts. 30-31 and Real Decreto 609/2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (notarized in country of origin) of each natural-person incorporator and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or police/passport authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the origin State is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Spanish Consular Office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record (antecedentes penales) issued within the three months preceding deed execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal-record authority of the country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (poder notarial) granted by each foreign incorporator or corporate shareholder for the incorporation procedure, including express authority to execute the deed, appoint administrators and open the corporate file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country of origin with raised and translated signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise Consular Legalization; the Spanish notary will keep the original on file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered residence and, if the shareholder is a legal entity, commercial registry extract, constitutional documents and last annual accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank, municipal population register or commercial registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation (traducción jurada) into Spanish of all foreign-language documents, including passport data, criminal records and powers of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator (traductor-intérprete jurado) certified by the Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required for the translation itself; the translator's signature is recorded by the Spanish notary at deed execution

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Companies Act), notably Articles 20, 22, 23, 58-62 and 210 (registered office, share capital, deed of incorporation, administrative body).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Mercantile Registry) of the province where the registered office is established; name reservation is processed through the Registro Mercantil Central.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) executed before a Spanish notary and thereafter registered in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SL must have a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid at incorporation; cash contributions must be evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate or notary deposit; no escrow account is required under Spanish law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The founder hereby subscribes and fully pays the entire share capital of EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 indivisible participations of EUR 1 each, and approves the articles of association as set forth in the public deed; (2) The registered office shall be established at [Address], Spain, and the administrative body is authorized to open bank accounts and to take all steps needed to obtain the tax identification number, register the company in the Mercantile Registry, and secure municipal operating licenses; (3) [Name and ID] is appointed sole administrator with all statutory powers, including representation before public and private bodies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Certificate of Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry) – online application at www.rmc.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application naming the proposed corporate name and up to two alternatives. The Certificate of Registration of Company Name confirms no identical name is already inscribed. The name reservation is valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Tax ID or passport of the founding partner
Proof of legal capacity of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is denied because of identity or similarity, file a new application with the next alternative name or appeal to the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Business Bank Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account in the name of 'S.L. en constitución', deposit at least EUR 3,000, and obtain a bank certificate attesting the deposit and the identifying details of each contributing partner.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of each founding partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional information, provide the draft deed and name certificate; if the bank refuses, open an account at another institution or deposit the capital through the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Deed of Incorporation Before Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) located in the province where the registered office will be situated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the name certificate, bank certificate, approved articles of association, and identification documents. The notary reviews the legality, reads the deed aloud, obtains signatures, and issues an original and certified copies of the escritura de constitución.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate from Registro Mercantil Central
Passport or NIE of all subscribers
Proof of address of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises defects, modify the deed or articles and re-execute; if the notary refuses authorization, the founders may correct the document and submit to another notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 036 to request the provisional corporate tax identification number within one month after execution of the deed, attaching the certified copy of the deed and the notary's certificate that registration has been applied for.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed of incorporation
Notarial certification that registration application is pending
Tax ID or passport of the administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended for missing information, provide the omitted document to the AEAT office and re-submit; no penalty applies if cured within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial corresponding to the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified copy of the notarial deed and the provisional NIF to the Mercantile Registry. The registrar reviews legal compliance, capital rules, articles of association, and appointment of administrators; upon approval the company is formally registered and acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the public deed of incorporation
First notarial copy of the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar suspends registration with a 'nota', submit correcting documents or modify the deed; after curing the observation, re-submit. The decision may be appealed to the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize Tax Registrations and Social Security Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription in the Mercantile Registry, obtain the definitive NIF by submitting Form 030/036, register the company for applicable corporate taxes and the Impuesto de Actividades Económicas (IAE), and enrol the administrators/employees with the social security system.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by the Mercantile Registry
Bank account details for direct debit of taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is delayed or incorrect, appear at the AEAT office with the registry certificate and the provisional NIF to obtain correction; social security discrepancies are cured by filing the appropriate affiliation forms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Licensing Authority (Ayuntamiento) – generally the Concejalía de Urbanismo, Actividades y Licencias of the municipality where the warehouse and packaging premises are located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Municipal de Actividad y Apertura (or Declaración Responsable de Apertura) for the operation of a warehouse and subscription-box packaging facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MTECO) and the environmental department of the corresponding Comunidad Autónoma.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Registration/Declaration (not full EIA) under Ley 21/2013, as the activity typically involves a small or medium warehouse below the thresholds requiring a full Environmental Impact Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewer ordinance discharge limits; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from packaging operations must stay below the applicable thresholds of Real Decreto 1042/2017; waste handling, including cardboard and plastics, must comply with Ley 7/2022 on waste and circular economy, including separation and proper disposal contracts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificado de protección contra incendios) and approved fire-fighting installations are required before opening; structural load inspection of the storage racking system must be certified; occupational risk prevention assessment (Riesgos Laborales) and the company's adherence to workplace safety rules under Ley 31/1995 are mandatory for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Tributaria. The AEAT administers the Spanish Tax Identification Number (NIF), Value Added Tax (VAT), Intrastat, and related national tax registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF from the AEAT, generally through Modelo 036, using the incorporation deed, articles of association, evidence of registered office, identification of directors and representatives, and duly legalized or apostilled and translated documents for foreign parties where applicable. Following registration of the deed with the competent Registro Mercantil, the company files the required information with the AEAT to obtain or confirm its definitive NIF. The Spanish NIF normally also serves as the domestic VAT identification number. An entity carrying out intra-Community acquisitions or supplies applies through Modelo 036 for registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI); the resulting VAT number is the NIF prefixed by 'ES' and is activated for VIES purposes after AEAT validation. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment may obtain an NIF through Modelo 036, directly or through an authorized representative. Non-EU businesses conducting Spanish VAT activities may generally be required to appoint a Spanish VAT representative, subject to applicable statutory exceptions and international arrangements. VAT registration must be completed before the relevant taxable activities commence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no Spanish equivalent of a general United States check-the-box election for an SL. A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person. Specific statutory regimes may be elected or applied if their conditions are met, including consolidated tax grouping, the special regime for entities in the Canary Islands where applicable, and other sector-specific regimes. Spanish and EU anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement ATAD measures and can deny deductions, tax exempt income, or impose inclusion consequences; they do not provide a general elective hybrid classification. A Spanish SL may also access VAT special regimes relevant to its activities, including the One-Stop Shop regimes for qualifying cross-border consumer supplies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, or IVA), governed principally by Law 37/1992. Spanish mainland and the Balearic Islands apply Spanish VAT; the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside the territorial scope of Spanish VAT and have separate indirect tax systems.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic VAT turnover threshold applies in Spain. A person carrying out an independent economic activity must generally register before commencing taxable operations, irrespective of turnover. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold is relevant to certain intra-EU business-to-consumer distance sales and electronically supplied, telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronic services, not to general Spanish domestic VAT registration. Qualifying EU consumer supplies may instead be reported through the Union OSS regime; qualifying imported consignments not exceeding EUR 150 may fall within IOSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for all private-sector invoices. Businesses within the Immediate Supply of Information (SII) regime, including entities with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, and REDEME-registered businesses, electronically submit prescribed VAT invoice-record data to the AEAT, generally within four business days, subject to statutory exceptions. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for transactions with Spanish public authorities under applicable public-procurement rules and uses required structured formats and platforms, including FACe where applicable. Law 18/2022 and its implementing framework establish phased private-sector B2B electronic-invoicing obligations, with detailed effective dates dependent on implementing regulations. Royal Decree 1007/2023 regulates compliant billing-record systems and the AEAT-facing requirements commonly referred to as VeriFactu, including integrity, traceability, preservation, and anti-tampering controls. A universal invoice-by-invoice digital stamp or real-time clearance requirement does not currently apply to every Spanish SL.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from the Spanish VAT territory to destinations outside the European Union may qualify for exemption with the right to deduct, economically equivalent to zero-rating, under Article 21 of Law 37/1992, provided the goods leave the VAT territory and the supplier retains reliable evidence of export and transport. The export declaration and customs exit confirmation, normally evidenced through the MRN, exit results, or equivalent customs records, are central evidence. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for exemption with the right to deduct under separate intra-Community supply rules when the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and required recapitulative and documentary conditions are met. Services supplied to business customers established outside Spain are generally outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rules, rather than technically zero-rated, subject to use-and-enjoyment rules and sector-specific exceptions. Consumer services require analysis of the applicable B2C place-of-supply rule. Export-related input VAT refunds require valid invoices, proof of taxable business activity, and compliance with the relevant periodic return or non-established-business refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) or equivalent export reference
Electronic customs exit confirmation, exit results, or equivalent evidence that the goods left the EU customs and VAT territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, and VAT treatment
Transport documentation, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or equivalent logistics evidence
Packing list and warehouse or carrier delivery records where necessary to reconcile the goods with the customs declaration
Proof of delivery or receipt by the non-EU customer where available
Payment records or other commercial evidence supporting the transaction and customer identity
For intra-Community supplies, the customer VAT identification number, transport evidence to another Member State, and required EC Sales List reporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds and no general 180-day repatriation rule applicable to Spanish VAT zero-rating. Export exemption depends on the substantive export and evidence requirements, not on a mandatory repatriation period. If the export is not proven, the AEAT may reassess Spanish VAT, deny related input-tax recovery or refund claims, and charge statutory late-payment interest. Deliberate or negligent incorrect VAT treatment may trigger penalties under General Tax Law 58/2003, including penalties commonly calculated as a percentage of unpaid tax, with aggravated cases potentially reaching 100% to 150% of the amount improperly omitted, depending on the infringement and circumstances. Incorrect or fraudulent invoicing may generate separate invoicing penalties. False customs declarations may also result in customs debt, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture measures, and potentially criminal liability for serious tax or customs fraud. Voluntary correction, complete transaction records, consistent customs data, and retention of evidence supporting exit, transport, customer identity, and accounting treatment are essential to reduce clawback exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acting as the competent central banking and macroprudential authority; foreign exchange and investment control processing is delegated to the Dirección General de Transacciones y Operaciones Exteriores (DGTOE) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Spain maintains complete liberalisation of capital and current account transactions under EU Treaty provisions (Articles 63-65 TFEU) and Royal Decree 1816/1991, as amended. Capital account transactions require ex-post statistical declarations to DGTOE for foreign direct investment where the participation reaches 10% or more or the value exceeds EUR 3,000,000; prior authorisation is not required. Profit remittance is unrestricted, but dividends paid by a Spanish SL to non-residents are subject to withholding tax under the Non-Resident Income Tax legislation (Royal Legislative Decree 5/2004) unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. No material exchange control hurdles exist for a subscription-box service operating through a Spanish SL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose mandatory export proceeds surrender or forced conversion ratios. Under Royal Decree 1816/1991 and Banco de España Circular 4/2012, exporters must report collections from foreign sales for balance-of-payments statistical purposes if the transaction value exceeds EUR 12,500. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained in authorised accounts or converted freely. No statutory conversion timeline applies. The exporter must submit the required declaration to Banco de España within the month following the transaction, retaining supporting commercial documentation for audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility with legal constraints. An EU/EEA Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensed under the Payment Services Directive (EU) 2015/2366 may passport into Spain and offer e-money accounts and payment services; however, it cannot fully substitute a Spanish resident bank account for all treasury functions, particularly for holding statutory corporate funds or for direct TARGET2 participation. Non-EU EMIs require a branch authorisation or must operate through a registered Spanish payment institution. For a Spanish SL, the recommended structure is a tier-1 Spanish bank account supplemented by a fintech EMI for high-speed cross-border disbursements and multicurrency float, subject to bank-approved remittance routing and client-money segregation rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Law 10/2010 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing and Royal Decree 304/2014, identification of the legal entity, directors, signatories and ultimate beneficial owners is mandatory. Physical presence of directors is not an absolute statutory requirement; banks may accept remote electronic identification using a qualified electronic signature under eIDAS Regulation (EU) 910/2014, video-identification with liveness verification, and notarised or apostilled corporate documents. For non-resident or politically exposed persons, many tier-1 banks will request a physical interview or a notarial/consular authentication step. For the subscription-box business, classified as standard low risk, remote onboarding is feasible if the beneficial ownership register (Registro Mercantil) is verified and source of funds documentation is provided. Final onboarding remains subject to each bank's internal KYC policies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain involving high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from the Registro de Titularidades Reales (Spanish beneficial ownership register); certified shareholding structure; notarised passports and proof of physical directors; CRS tax residence declarations; evidence of real economic activity in Spain including local payroll, leased warehouse, and supplier contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large expected inbound capital injection to the escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital increase deed formalised before a Spanish notary and registered in the Registro Mercantil; board/shareholder resolution authorising the capital contribution; bank reference letter from the remitting institution; source of wealth statement for non-resident investors; intermediary payment chain disclosure and transfer purpose documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anticipated cross-border payout concentration to merchants or logistics providers in sanction-list exposed regions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU restrictive measures and OFAC screening certificates for all counterparties; transaction-level commercial invoices and contracts; shipping and logistics documentation including CN22 or airway bills and customs declarations; e-commerce marketplace agreements; annual AML compliance certification proving continuous monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared ISIC 4791 activity and corporate financial flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified tax residency certificate; Spanish tax filings (Modelo 200 and Modelo 390); IAE census extract; detailed subscription-box business plan with revenue recognition policy; host-to-country intercompany agreements showing commercial substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funding must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's bank to the SL's euro-denominated account in Spain. The wire should contain the EU/FDI purpose code for foreign direct investment, with full remittance information in field 70, referencing the underlying investment declaration. Where the investment exceeds EUR 3,000,000 or the participation threshold is reached after the operation, the SL must file the online DGTOE foreign direct investment declaration within one month of formalisation. Verification is performed by the receiving bank through sanctions screening, beneficial ownership matching, and confirmation that the inbound credit matches the filed investment structure. Sterling, US-dollar and Latin American currency cables may be accepted through correspondent banks and converted into EUR on arrival, always respecting the declared purpose and FX compliance checks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier, logistics and marketing payments should be executed through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers using SEPA rails for euro-denominated domestic settlements and correspondent banking for non-EU trade creditors. For larger subscription-box merchandise procurements, commercial letters of credit under ICC UCP600 are permissible; presentation documents must comply with ISBP 745 to avoid discrepancies. The remittance field 70 must contain the applicable trade in goods or services purpose code and reference the underlying commercial invoice. Parties should use TARGET2 settlement for intraday euro flows and leverage Spanish banking APIs for automatic reconciliation. For Latin American vendor payouts, prudent treasury practice uses segregated multicurrency accounts held in the Spanish bank or through an EMI partner, with NDF execution as required for currencies lacking onshore deliverability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/LATAM currency forwards) up to 12-month tenor
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted Latin American currencies where onshore FX conversion is unavailable or non-tradeable
FX swap and rollover contracts for short-term cross-currency liquidity management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for medium-term balance-sheet hedging of funding liabilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts (Cuentas Anuales) with the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) corresponding to the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The shareholders' meeting must approve the annual accounts within six months of the financial year-end; the approved accounts must be filed with the Mercantile Registry within one month after approval. For a calendar-year SL, approval is due no later than 30 June and deposit is commonly due no later than 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit triggers closure of the company's corporate file (cierre registral), preventing the registration of subsequent corporate deeds; non-deposit for two consecutive financial years causes the Mercantile Registry to close the registration sheet. There is no automatic administrative strike-off, but prolonged closure blocks all public filings and may lead to judicial dissolution at the request of the tax authority or affected parties; directors may incur liability for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 25 days after the six-month period following the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year entity, no later than 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment triggers late-filing surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% depending on the delay, plus late-payment interest. AEAT may assess the tax using partial or estimated data. Persistent non-filing and non-payment can lead to enforcement of assessed liabilities, director liability, and forfeiture of tax benefits; it does not by itself trigger administrative strike-off under mercantile law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual third-party transactions information return (Modelo 347), if any supplier or customer transactions exceed EUR 3,005.06 in the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing opens on 1 February and closes on 28 February (or 29 February in a leap year) for the preceding calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, inaccurate or incomplete submissions are subject to penalties under the General Tax Law, with a minimum penalty of EUR 300 for incorrect data and penalties that can reach 75% of the relevant amounts, plus late-payment interest. Administrative strike-off is not a direct tax consequence, but continued non-compliance intensifies tax enforcement actions against the entity and directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Electronic legalization of statutory accounting books (Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) via electronic legalization procedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year; for calendar-year books, submission for legalization must be completed no later than 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books have reduced evidentiary value in commercial proceedings and may be rejected for certain corporate filings; record-keeping failures can be penalized by the tax administration under the General Tax Law. The registry does not administratively strike off the company for this default, but the defect may impair annual accounts deposit and contribute to registry closure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent registered auditor is required when, for two consecutive financial years, the SL meets at least two of the following criteria: total assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average annual number of employees exceeds 50. An audit may also be required by shareholders representing at least 5% of the share capital, by sector-specific rules, or by the terms of financing agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP in accordance with the Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC) and the Spanish Capital Companies Act; IFRS as adopted by the EU is required for consolidated accounts of listed groups and is not generally required for a non-listed SL in ISIC 4791 subscription box merchandising.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing. The SL must maintain its beneficial ownership record in the Registro de Titularidades Reales at the Mercantile Registry and file any change of direct or indirect ownership or control within one month after the corresponding corporate deed is registered. Share transfers must be formalized in a notarial deed and recorded in the Libro Registro de Socios; there is no annual reappointment or re-declaration calendar for UBO data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Partners)
Libro de Actas de la Junta General (Minute Book of General Meetings)
Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales (Inventory and Annual Accounts Ledger)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Spanish corporate income tax rate. Qualifying newly created entities generally apply 15% in the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. Qualifying start-up companies may apply 15% during the period in which start-up status is obtained and the following three tax periods, subject to conditions. Special reduced rates for micro-enterprises and small entities are subject to turnover thresholds and phased statutory changes; confirm the rate for the relevant tax year.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential relief includes the 15% rate for qualifying new entities and certified start-ups; tax credits for qualifying R&D and technological innovation, audiovisual productions, and certain other activities; and deductions for qualifying capitalisation and job-creation measures. Eligibility, limits, documentation, and carryforward rules depend on the specific incentive. No general tax holiday applies to an ordinary Spanish SL.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed expiry: tax loss carryforwards generally may be carried forward indefinitely. Annual use is subject to statutory percentage limits, with a minimum offset generally available up to EUR 1 million, and additional restrictions for changes in ownership, dormant entities, and certain reorganisations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (annual Corporate Income Tax return), filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) e-Office. Modelo 202 is generally used for advance payments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 200: Annual. Modelo 202: Generally three advance-payment periods each year, subject to the taxpayer's status and statutory rules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual deadline is 25 July. Modelo 202: Generally 1–20 April, October, and December; the precise deadline and payment calculation depend on the applicable statutory method and calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Identification and tax-period fields (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's Spanish tax identification number, legal name, registered address, tax period, activity information, and return type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not change the SL's Spanish resident corporate-tax filing obligation. Use the SL's Spanish NIF and registered details; disclose shareholder information where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax regime and entity-status fields (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select the applicable corporate-tax regime and indicate eligibility for any reduced rate, special regime, or tax incentive claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim a reduced rate solely because ownership is non-resident. Retain evidence supporting any start-up, new-entity, micro-enterprise, or other special-rate eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Accounting result and taxable-base reconciliation (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting profit or loss and reconcile it to the tax base for permanent and temporary differences, nondeductible expenses, tax-exempt income, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish tax rules to the SL's worldwide income as a Spanish tax-resident entity. Separately assess withholding, permanent-establishment, and treaty issues for payments to non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Loss carryforwards and tax-base reductions (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report available tax loss carryforwards and claimed reductions, applying applicable ordering, annual limits, and anti-abuse restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain records establishing the origin, amount, and availability of losses. A shareholder change or restructuring may restrict their use.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate, credits, and tax liability (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the rate for the relevant period, calculate gross tax, and claim eligible deductions and credits subject to their statutory limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the rate applicable to the SL and tax year, not the shareholder's residence-country rate. Support each credit and preferential rate with contemporaneous evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholdings, advance payments, and final balance (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit eligible Spanish withholdings and Modelo 202 payments, calculate the balance payable or refundable, and select the permitted payment or refund method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Spanish withholdings to certificates and accounting records. Foreign tax credits require qualifying foreign tax and supporting documentation under Spanish law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a prior tax-authority requirement generally attracts a surcharge under the General Tax Law, normally 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay, capped at 12% before interest rules apply; delay beyond 12 months generally attracts a 15% surcharge plus late-payment interest. If the authority has required filing, fixed or percentage penalties may apply, commonly 50%–150% of the unpaid amount depending on culpability and aggravating factors. Late payment, inaccurate returns, and failure to make required advance payments can trigger separate surcharges, interest, or penalties. Voluntary correction before notification may reduce exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 (advance corporate income tax payment), filed and paid electronically through the AEAT e-Office when required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Generally three times per year: April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1–20 April, October, and December, subject to the official calendar and applicable calculation method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxpayer identification and period (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's NIF, legal name, and relevant advance-payment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's own tax identification and details regardless of the residence of its shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Calculation method and payment base (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the applicable statutory calculation method and report the required tax base or prior-period tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the method legally required for the SL, including any turnover-based mandatory method; do not substitute the shareholder's tax position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Advance payment and payment details (codes vary by annual form version)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the instalment, apply only permitted credits or adjustments, and submit payment using an available AEAT-authorised payment method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain the electronic submission receipt and payment evidence. Reconcile all instalments to the annual Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to pay or file required advance payments may result in late-payment surcharges, interest, or penalties under the General Tax Law. Penalty treatment depends on whether the taxpayer files voluntarily or after an authority requirement, the amount unpaid, and the circumstances.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish domestic withholding on dividends paid to non-residents, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. A qualifying EU parent may obtain exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in Spain, generally requiring a qualifying holding (normally at least 5%, or the statutory acquisition-cost alternative), minimum holding period, eligible form and tax status, and anti-abuse compliance. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the Spanish payer with a current certificate of tax residence issued by the competent authority, normally apostilled or legalised only if required, and evidence of beneficial ownership and entitlement to the claimed treaty or EU exemption. The payer applies the domestic exemption or treaty rate only when statutory documentation and conditions are satisfied; otherwise it generally withholds at the domestic rate. The payer files the applicable withholding return, commonly Modelo 216, and annual summary Modelo 296. A recipient may claim a refund from the AEAT for excess withholding, subject to limitation periods and supporting evidence. Treaty forms, validity periods, and procedural requirements depend on the relevant treaty and current AEAT instructions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Spanish non-resident income tax withholding rate on Spanish-source royalties and interest paid to non-residents is generally 19%, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. Qualifying interest and royalties paid to associated companies in other EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, subject to qualifying legal forms, tax residence and liability, beneficial ownership, minimum direct holding conditions, and anti-abuse rules. Applicable tax-treaty rates vary by country and payment category; confirm the relevant treaty before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spanish related-party transactions must generally be valued at arm's length and documented. The full documentation obligation is generally relieved for transactions with the same related party whose aggregate consideration does not exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period, subject to statutory exceptions. Simplified documentation may apply to entities or groups with net turnover below EUR 45 million, subject to exclusions. Master File requirements generally apply to groups with consolidated net turnover of at least EUR 45 million. Additional country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Spanish transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, controlled-foreign-company, permanent-establishment, and tax-residence rules may nevertheless challenge arrangements lacking commercial rationale, personnel, decision-making, or functions consistent with reported income. A Spanish SL should maintain evidence of its actual management, operations, contractual functions, assets, and risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion and fraudulent returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable sales, fabricating expenses or invoices, omitting income, or using false records to reduce tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the tax shortfall, depending on the infringement and aggravating circumstances, in addition to tax and interest. Tax fraud may constitute a criminal offence where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period; the basic criminal penalty may include imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated cases may carry higher penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability where they personally participate in or authorise fraud, and may incur civil or tax liability under statutory conditions for their own conduct or failure to perform legal duties. Imprisonment and ancillary disqualifications may apply following criminal conviction. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party goods, services, financing, intellectual property, or cost allocations other than at arm's length; failing to prepare or retain required documentation; or providing inaccurate documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may adjust taxable income and assess tax and interest. Specific documentation and reporting failures may attract fixed penalties, including amounts calculated per missing or incorrect data item, subject to statutory caps; an adjustment without a qualifying tax shortfall may also trigger a penalty calculated by reference to the adjustment. Exact exposure depends on the infringement, documentation, and tax result.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically personally liable for the SL's transfer-pricing tax debt. Liability may arise under statutory derivation rules for culpable participation, obstruction, or breach of duties, and criminal liability may apply where conduct forms part of tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting fictitious invoices, suppressing subscription sales, falsely claiming input VAT, or misrepresenting cross-border goods movements or consumer transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessments, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties apply; serious or very serious infringements can carry substantial percentage-based fines. Conduct meeting the criminal tax-fraud threshold or constituting document fraud may also lead to criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal or derivative liability may apply where a director knowingly directs, facilitates, or conceals the conduct. The SL's limited-liability form does not protect a director from liability for personal wrongdoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared payroll, social security, or worker misclassification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating employees as independent contractors to avoid payroll withholding or social-security contributions, failing to register workers, or concealing remuneration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back taxes, social-security contributions, surcharges, interest, and administrative fines may apply. Serious cases can result in criminal liability under applicable Spanish tax, social-security, or labour offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable where statutory requirements for derivative liability or criminal participation are met. Imprisonment is possible for qualifying criminal conduct; it is not an automatic consequence of an administrative assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and suspicious payment flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly processing proceeds of crime, concealing beneficial ownership, accepting unexplained third-party subscription payments, or failing applicable AML duties where the SL is a regulated obliged entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money-laundering offences may result in imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and ancillary measures under Spanish criminal law. Administrative AML sanctions depend on whether the business is an obliged entity and on the breach; ordinary retail subscription activity does not by itself make the SL an AML-obliged entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may face personal criminal liability for knowing participation, concealment, or serious supervisory failures where the legal elements are met. Corporate criminal liability may also arise for qualifying offences committed for the company's benefit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SL as a nominal entity to obtain treaty benefits or deductions without genuine commercial functions, decision-making, or beneficial ownership, or to conceal the true recipient of income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may deny treaty or domestic-law benefits, recharacterise transactions, adjust taxable income, and assess tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Criminal consequences require conduct meeting the elements and thresholds of a criminal offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for deliberate fraud, false declarations, or culpable breach of statutory duties. Limited liability is not automatically disregarded merely because the company has limited operations or foreign shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain corporate and tax records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to keep accounting books, invoices, related-party documentation, payment evidence, or records required to substantiate deductions and returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may reject unsupported deductions or credits and impose statutory recordkeeping, reporting, or tax-return penalties, with tax, interest, and further penalties where an underpayment results.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal or derivative liability where their own conduct satisfies statutory conditions, including intentional destruction or concealment of records. A filing or recordkeeping breach alone does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.
